original_value: AbstractThe explosive growth of network data traffic puts new demands on traffic scheduling. In this paper, the scheduling algorithm based on the software-defined network (SDN) architecture is studied. Firstly, the SDN architecture was introduced, then an SDN-based adaptive multi-path load balancing algorithm was proposed and finally the algorithm was simulated on the Mininet simulation platform to compare the performance of the proposed algorithm and traditional equal-cost multi-path routing algorithm by using Ryu as the controller. It was found that the proposed algorithm had greater throughput, higher bandwidth utilization and shorter transmission time in allocation scheduling of network data traffic, which could effectively reduce network congestion and ensure the reliability of the network. This study verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method in allocation scheduling of network data traffic and provides some theoretical bases for the further application of the SDN architecture-based allocation scheduling algorithm.

result.paraphrase: Abstract The rapid increase in network data traffic creates new requirements for traffic scheduling. This paper examines a scheduling algorithm based on the software-defined network (SDN) architecture. First, the SDN architecture is introduced; then an SDN-based adaptive multi-path load-balancing algorithm is proposed; finally, the algorithm is simulated on the Mininet platform, using Ryu as the controller, to compare its performance with the traditional equal-cost multi-path routing algorithm. The results show that the proposed algorithm achieves higher throughput, better bandwidth utilization, and shorter transmission time in network data traffic allocation scheduling, which can effectively reduce network congestion and ensure network reliability. This study confirms the effectiveness of the proposed method for network data traffic allocation scheduling and offers a theoretical basis for the further application of SDN architecture-based scheduling algorithms.
